title: Cord prolapse
summary: Umbilical cord palpated or visible below/alongside the presenting part, membranes ruptured.

cord-outcome.title: Cord prolapse — emergency drill
actions: Call for emergency help immediately — obstetric, anaesthetic and neonatal teams; category 1 caesarean unless imminent vaginal birth.
Minimise handling of the cord; if outside the vagina, keep it warm and moist but do not push it back in.

Relieve pressure on the cord: manually elevate the presenting part with a hand in the vagina, and/or knee-chest or exaggerated Sitting-Trendelenburg/left-lateral with hips elevated — VERIFY preferred local positioning technique.
Consider filling the maternal bladder (via catheter) to further elevate the presenting part if transfer is required — VERIFY local protocol for volume.
Continuous fetal monitoring if available without delaying transfer/delivery.
Tocolysis may be considered by the obstetric team to reduce contractions while preparing for birth — VERIFY local protocol.
Move rapidly to theatre — do not delay transfer to attempt non-essential steps.
cord-outcome.phoneScript: If this is identified during a home assessment or the woman describes feeling something in the vagina after membranes rupture: call 999 immediately, advise the knee-chest position, and stay on the line for further instructions while the ambulance is en route.
documentationPrompts: Fetal heart rate at identification and subsequently.
Time of emergency call and time of birth.
